Constructor Detail

ModifiedCholeskyLeftDecomposition

public ModifiedCholeskyLeftDecomposition(cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix2D A)

From a symmetric, positive definite matrix A, constructs a 'safely' positive definite Cholesky Left decomposition using the methods described in "Algorithm 695 , collected algorithms from ACM. Transactions on mathematical software, Vol. 17, no. 3, September, 1991, pp. 306-312." Guaranteed to rescue you if the matrix is ill-conditioned or not quite positive definite.

The decomposition is of form PT.A.P = L.LT

The permutation P is available through getPermutation(), and the factor L in getL()

Example Usage:

      // set up some matrix A....,then
      chol = new ModifiedCholeskyLeftDecomposition(A);
          // or, for wierdly scaled matrices
      chol = new ModifiedCholeskyLeftDecomposition(A,true);
          L = chol.getL();
      int[] p = chol.getPermutation();
      // form B = L.LT using the COLT Blas routines
      B = L.like(); 
      cern.colt.matrix.linalg.Blas blas = cern.colt.matrix.linalg.SeqBlas.seqBlas;
      // form  L.LT
      blas.dgemm(false,true,1.0,L,L,0,B);
      // unpermute to form  P.L.LT.PT which should look like A
      for (i=0;i< n;i++) {
        for (j=0;j < n;j++) {
          tmp = B.getQuick(i,j);
          A.setQuick(p[i],p[j],tmp);
        }
      }
      System.out.println(A.toString());

Parameters:
A - Square matrix: Positive definite or close thereto.
Throws:
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if A is not square.

ModifiedCholeskyLeftDecomposition

public ModifiedCholeskyLeftDecomposition(cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix2D A,
                                         boolean preScale,
                                         boolean scaleWithinMachEpsRange)
Same as ModifiedCholeskyLeftDecomposition(), except if preScale==true, the matrix is scaled by the diagonal before decomposition, and the scale vector is used to rescale L after the decomposition. If scaleWithinMachEpsRange==true, scaling applies to rows j whose diagonal element satisfies |A_jj| > machine_eps * max(A_ii), i.e. within a factor of say 10^-16. Smaller numbers are assumed to best noise and are unscaled. If scaleWithinMachEpsRange==false, no thresholding on scaling applies, and all diagonal elemnets are used. Zeros are scaled as if 1, though.

getPermutation

public int[] getPermutation()
Call this to obtain the permutation P performed in the decomposition. If unpermuted, the vector getPermutation() will be {0,1,2,3,,...} The length of the permutation is A.rows().

                                             cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix1D b)
After the Cholesky Decomposition is instantiated, we can solve the linear problem A.x=b using this call. If x==null when called a new vector is returned with the solution, else the solution is written in place into the provided x

getInverseViaCholesky

public static cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix2D getInverseViaCholesky(cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix2D C)
Returns the inverse of the original matrix. using the decomposition

C=L.L^T, so

C^{-1} = (L^{-1})^T.L^{-1}

Typical calling sequence is 

         DoubleMatrix2D Ainv = D.getInverseViaCholesky(L);

Parameters:
L - square matrix
Throws:
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if L is not square.

getCholeskyLeftInverse

public static void getCholeskyLeftInverse(cern.colt.matrix.DoubleMatrix2D L)
Returns the inverse of the left Cholesky matrix L *in place*. Typical calling sequence is 
         ModifiedCholeskyLeftDecomposition D = ModifiedCholeskyLeftDecomposition(A); 
         DoubleMatrix2D R = D.getL();
         D.getCholeskyLeftInverse(R);
Can be called with any Cholesky factor L

Parameters:
L - square lower triangular matrix (usually obtained from getL())
Throws:
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if L is not square.
